title: Wrath of God
definition: The Wrath of God is His holy and just opposition to sin, evil, rebellion, and all that destroys what He loves.
summary: The Wrath of God is His holy and just opposition to sin, evil, rebellion, and all that destroys what He loves.
christFocus: Jesus bore wrath for sinners at the cross, showing both the seriousness of sin and the depth of God's saving mercy.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God's wrath is not sinful rage or uncontrolled anger. It is His settled, holy opposition to evil. Because God is good, He cannot be indifferent toward sin, oppression, abuse, idolatry, deception, or rebellion.

Scripture's teaching on wrath shows why salvation is necessary. Sinners do not merely need encouragement; they need rescue from guilt, judgment, and separation from God.

At the cross, Christ stands in the place of sinners. God's justice is not denied, and mercy is not cheap. The wrath of God makes the grace of God shine with holy weight.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people want a God of love who never judges evil, but a God who never judges evil would not be loving to the wounded, oppressed, or abused. God's wrath assures believers that evil matters and justice is real.

This doctrine also keeps the Gospel clear. Jesus did not die merely to inspire us; He died to save us from sin and judgment and bring us to God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not run from the truth of God's wrath; run to Christ who bore wrath for sinners. Let this doctrine deepen repentance, gratitude, worship, evangelism, and compassion for people who still need the Savior.
